content: 1. Administer zidovudine intravenously at a dose of 5 mg/kg every 6 hours for a duration of 4 to 6 weeks, as determined by the patient's risk factors. For further guidance, consultation is available through the National Perinatal HIV Hotline at 888-448-8765. Monitor the patient's complete blood count (CBC) and hemoglobin (Hgb) levels during treatment. 2. The combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF constitutes a complete antiretroviral regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretroviral agents. This combination is contraindicated in such scenarios. 3. Zidovudine and atidarsagene autotemcel: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued for at least one month prior to cell mobilization or for the expected duration required for the elimination of these medications. 4. Zidovudine and betibeglogene autotemcel: ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. 5. Cidofovir and zidovudine: Co-administration with probenecid may reduce zidovudine clearance. Reduce the zidovudine dose by 50% on days when cidofovir and probenecid are administered together. 6. Clozapine and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Deferiprone and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of neutropenia or agranulocytosis. Avoid this combination if possible, or monitor the absolute neutrophil count more frequently. 8. Elivaldogene autotemcel and zidovudine: ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before initiating medications for stem cell mobilization, for the duration of the medications' elimination, and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 9. Ganciclovir and zidovudine: Co-administration is contraindicated due to increased toxicity from pharmacodynamic synergy. 10. Zidovudine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel: ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for complete elimination. 11. Ribavirin and zidovudine: Ribavirin reduces the efficacy of zidovudine by competing for thymidine kinase during conversion to its active form. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Ropinterferon alfa-2b and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to additive effects of myelosuppressive agents. Monitor patients closely for excessive myelosuppression. 13. Valganciclovir and zidovudine: Co-administration is contraindicated due to increased toxicity from pharmacodynamic synergy. 14. Abacavir and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 15. Acalabrutinib and zidovudine: Co-administration may increase the risk of myelosuppressive effects. Use with caution and monitor closely. 16. Atazanavir and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 17. Azathioprine and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 18. Carboplatin and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 19. Cisplatin and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 20. Clarithromycin and zidovudine: Clarithromycin may increase or decrease zidovudine levels through an unknown mechanism. Separate administration by at least 2 to 4 hours and monitor closely. 21. Clofarabine and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 22. Conivaptan and zidovudine: Conivaptan increases zidovudine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 23. Dasatinib and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 24. Dexrazoxane and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 25. Doxorubicin and zidovudine: Co-administration should be avoided due to an antagonistic relationship demonstrated in vitro. 26. Efavirenz and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 27. Emtricitabine and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 28. Enfuvirtide and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 29. Fosamprenavir and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 30. Hydroxyurea and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 31. Ibritumomab tiuxetan and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 32. Ifosfamide and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor for increased toxicities. 33. Imatinib and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 34. Indinavir and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 35. Interferon alfa-2b and zidovudine: Co-administration increases zidovudine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor for increased myelosuppression and liver decompensation. 36. Interferon beta-1a and zidovudine: Co-administration increases zidovudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. Monitor for increased myelosuppression and liver decompensation. 37. Ketoconazole and zidovudine: Ketoconazole increases zidovudine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 38. Lamivudine and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 39. Lenalidomide and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 40. Methotrexate and zidovudine: Co-administration increases the risk of myelosuppression due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use with caution and monitor closely. 41. Nelfinavir and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 42. Nevirapine and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 43. Orlistat and zidovudine: Orlistat decreases zidovudine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if virological control is lost. 44. Rifampin and zidovudine: Rifampin decreases zidovudine levels by increasing its metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 45. Ritonavir and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 46. Tenofovir DF and zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use with caution and monitor closely. 47. Tipranavir and zidovudine: Tipranavir decreases zidovudine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 48. Trimethoprim and zidovudine: Trimethoprim increases zidovudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. 49. Valproic acid and zidovudine: Valproic acid increases zidovudine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 50. Zidovudine and amphotericin B deoxycholate: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely. 51. Zidovudine and dapsone: Co-administration increases bone marrow toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely. 52. Zidovudine and fluconazole: Fluconazole increases zidovudine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor closely. 53. Zidovudine and methadone: Methadone increases zidovudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. Monitor closely. 54. Zidovudine and pyrimethamine: Co-administration increases bone marrow toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely. 55. Zidovudine and sulfamethoxazole: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely. 56. Zidovudine and valacyclovir: Co-administration increases zidovudine effects through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for lethargy and fatigue. 57. Zidovudine and vinblastine: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely. 58. Zidovudine and vincristine: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely. 59. Zidovudine and vincristine liposomal: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely.
